title: Timers and a clean unload
description:
Write the timer arithmetic of lesson 3.04, and a checker for the order of the clean-up steps in `Unload`:

```cpp
std::int64_t relativeDue(std::int64_t milliseconds);                     // for KeSetTimerEx: negative, 100 ns units
std::int64_t msUntilFire(std::int64_t due, std::int64_t nowFileTime);    // 0 if already due
int firesBetween(std::int64_t firstMs, int periodMs, std::int64_t fromMs, std::int64_t toMs);
std::string checkUnload(const std::vector<std::string>& steps);
```

- `relativeDue(1000)` is `-10 000 000`. For zero or negative milliseconds the formula would give 0 or a positive number, which means an absolute time long past: return `-1` instead (the smallest relative wait).
- `msUntilFire`: a negative `due` is relative: `-due / 10000` milliseconds (rounded down). A positive one is an absolute FILETIME: `(due - now) / 10000` if in the future, else 0.
- `firesBetween`: a timer first fires at `firstMs` and then every `periodMs` (0 means once). How many times does it fire with `fromMs < t <= toMs`?
- `checkUnload`: the steps are names among `cancel timer`, `flush dpcs`, `wait work items`, `free context`, `delete link`, `delete device`. Rules, reported as the first broken one: `flush dpcs` must come after `cancel timer` (`"flush dpcs before cancel timer"`); `free context` must come after both `flush dpcs` and `wait work items` (`"free context before flush dpcs"` / `"free context before wait work items"`, checked in that order); `delete device` must come after `delete link` (`"delete device before delete link"`); every one of the six must appear exactly once (`"missing <step>"` / `"twice <step>"`, checked first, in the list order above). `""` if all is well.
hints: For `firesBetween`, count the fires up to `to` and subtract the fires up to `from`; "fires at or before t" is `(t - first) / period + 1` once `t >= first`.
